transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Eden CTO), Sam Rivera (Lead ML Eng), Priya Desai (Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining—i'm maya from redwood, this is arjun on the engineering side, we'll walk through our hosted api for chat and text generation, keep it practical, show streaming and params and a bit about retries.
[00:12] Laura Kim: great, thanks. quick context: we're building a care-coordinator assistant to draft messages and triage patient intents; latency needs to be <600ms median for short replies, and we have strict PII rules.
[00:25] Sam Rivera: and we send bursts — mornings spike — so curious about burst capacity and cost.
[00:34] Arjun Patel: totally, we'll show the SDK examples that handle streaming tokens, and we can talk about batching for cost. a quick agenda — demo the console call, code sample for streaming with retry/backoff, param tuning, then Q&A.

[00:48] (screen share starts)
[01:05] Arjun Patel: opening the hosted api tab — here is a simple chat call, notice the stream flag; streaming gives you token-by-token events which is good for UI latency, you can pipe partial responses to the client. code snippet: 
    // pseudo js snippet shown
    const res = client.chat.create({ model: 'rw-chat-1', messages, stream: true });
    res.on('data', chunk => renderToken(chunk));
    // example shows how to cancel mid-response

[02:10] Sam Rivera: does stream guarantee ordering? if we reconnect mid-response do we get duplicates?
[02:20] Arjun Patel: good q. ordering is preserved per request, duplicates can happen if a client retries incorrectly; best practice is to use an idempotency key per logical user-turn and apply dedupe client-side. we also expose sequence indices in stream events to reconcile.
[02:45] Priya Desai: is that documented? we need to show SRE and security how to validate transcripts.
[02:53] Arjun Patel: yes, we'll share the streaming contract doc and example replay/dedupe patterns. action item for me.

[03:10] Maya Chen: now quick note on params — temperature, top_p, max_tokens, presence/ frequency penalties. lowering temperature and top_p reduces variance and helps keep generated text more deterministic, which sounds relevant for clinical messaging.
[03:34] Sam Rivera: what's the recommended default for something like message rewriting? we want short, precise replies.
[03:40] Arjun Patel: start with temperature 0.0-0.3, top_p 0.8-0.95, max_tokens tuned to expected reply length, presence penalty 0 to discourage repetition. in the console we show token preview to estimate cost.

[04:12] Laura Kim: cost — how do we think about streaming vs non-streaming for cost?
[04:20] Maya Chen: streaming is billed same per-token; it helps UX because tokens arrive earlier, but it doesn't reduce token count. cost optimizations are via batching requests, caching common prefixes, or using a smaller model for deterministic formatting.

[04:45] (demo flips to console analytics)
[05:00] Arjun Patel: here's the per-route cost breakdown, tokens in vs tokens out, and latency percentiles. you can set routing policies to fallback to a cheaper model when latency SLOs allow.

[05:30] Sam Rivera: for bursts — will hosted API autoscale? do we need Dedicated?
[05:38] Maya Chen: hosted autoscaling handles typical bursts; we also offer burst credits for predictable spikes. Dedicated is recommended when you need guaranteed throughput and isolation. we can model your traffic and show cost delta in the PoC.

[06:05] Priya Desai: security — do you support KMS and customer-managed keys? what about logs and retention?
[06:13] Arjun Patel: yes, for Private we support customer KMS fully; hosted supports envelope encryption and managed KMS with options for restricted retention and audit logs. we'll share SOC2 and encryption docs — but note if you require full KMS control + VPC egress rules, Private or Dedicated private control plane is the path.
[06:40] Laura Kim: our compliance team will want to see the SOC2 report and attestations, and specifically audits for access to logs.
[06:48] Maya Chen: noted — Arjun will send the security package.

[07:10] (walking through a code retry example)
[07:25] Arjun Patel: here is a retry/backoff snippet. important: treat generative calls as non-idempotent unless you set an idempotency key for the logical turn. we recommend exponential backoff with jitter and check the request status endpoint for long-running tasks. if a stream is interrupted, client should reconcile using the sequence markers.
[08:05] Sam Rivera: can you show an example in python?
[08:10] Arjun Patel: yep — shows python example with requests/SDK, using a unique message_id header and local dedupe store. also shows how to truncate last partial token and ask for continuation rather than re-requesting from scratch.

[09:00] Laura Kim: how do we handle PII? we will be sending some de-identified patient text but want guaranteed deletion policies.
[09:08] Arjun Patel: hosted has configurable retention windows and can disable logging for certain routes; for strict no-logs you should look at Private deployments. encryption at rest and in transit is standard; we can show how to redact client-side and use tokenization techniques.

[09:40] Maya Chen: quick perf note — for short replies (<=60 tokens) latency depends a lot on cold start and batching; we tune runtime kernels for low latency but at high throughput you benefit from batching. we can run benchmarks with your payload to see tradeoffs.

[10:05] (demo of Optimize suggestions)
[10:12] Arjun Patel: here's Redwood Optimize — it looks at your traffic patterns and suggests batching thresholds, quantization choices, and recommended model variants per route. Optimize also surfaces quality regressions against a prompt set. you can tie alerts to evals in the console.
[11:00] Sam Rivera: interesting — can Optimize automatically switch models on degradation?
[11:06] Arjun Patel: you can set rollout policies — canary, auto-fallback to a stable model if quality drops or latency breaches SLO. we showed a similar flow for a retail customer last month.

[12:00] (questions from Priya about auditability)
[12:10] Priya Desai: will we have per-request audit logs that show who accessed what and when?
[12:18] Arjun Patel: yes, token-level tracing and request metadata are available; in Private you can ship logs to your SIEM. hosted keeps an audit trail and RBAC controls.

[12:45] Laura Kim: timeline — if PoC looks good we want production in Q1 2027, ideally starting hosted then evaluating Dedicated.
[12:55] Maya Chen: sounds reasonable; PoC this month, then ramp.

[13:10] (walkthrough ends, recap)
[13:15] Maya Chen: recap — we'll send pricing and security docs, arjun to share streaming/retry examples, eden to send sanitized dataset, schedule a 2hr benchmark. any other open items?
[13:30] Sam Rivera: nothing else, just to confirm — on billing, is there a way to cap daily spend?
[13:36] Maya Chen: yes you can set quotas per API key and per-route spend caps. we'll include config steps in the follow-up.

[13:50] Laura Kim: thanks — this was useful.
[13:55] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email.
